thread_title: Antibody Production: Scale and Cellular Requirements
narrative_summary: Human antibody production is remarkable in scale: over one million different antibody specificities can be generated from a daily production of 2.5 billion pro-B cells, which mature into functional B cells.
root_concept: Production of different antibodies in humans
terminal_concepts: over one million different specific antibodies

thread_title: B Cell Development: Progenitor Stage Progression
narrative_summary: B cell development proceeds through ordered stages: bone marrow stem cells differentiate into early pro-B cells, which undergo D-J rearrangement to become late pro-B cells. Subsequent V-DJ rearrangement produces large pre-B cells, followed by light chain rearrangement in small pre-B cells, culminating in immature B cells expressing surface IgM. Final maturation results in circulating B cells co-expressing IgM and IgD.
